Author: Anil Verma

1  IN THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE  BEFORE  HON'BLE SHRI JUSTICE ANIL VERMA  ON THE 18 th OF DECEMBER, 2023  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 29456 of 2023  BETWEEN:-
 VICTIM X/ PROSECUTRIX THROUGH POLICE STATION  INDUSTRIAL AREA DEWAS (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI NILESH DAVE - ADVOCATE)
 AND  1. PRASOON S/O SANDEEP CHATURVEDI, AGED 31  YEARS, R/O 176 BAJRANG NAGAR DISTT. DEWAS  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 2. STATE OF M.P. THROUGH P.S. INDUSTRIAL AREA,
 DEWAS DIST. DEWAS (MADHYA PRADESH)
 .
 (MS. SARIKA ATHALE- ADVOCATE FOR RESPONDENT NO.1)

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH  AT INDORE
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
ORDER Both the parties heard.

2. Applicant/complainant has filed this petition under section 439(2) of Cr.P.C. for cancellation of bail granted to respondent no. 1/accused by trial court vide order dated 14.12.2022 in bail application No. 905/2022.
3.
As per prosecution story, prosecutrix/victim lodged an FIR at police station Industrial Area Dwas against respondent no. 1.

Accordingly offence under sections 376, 376(2)(n), 342, 294, 323, 506,
312, 386 and 509 of IPC vide crime No. 705/2022 was registered.
Vide order dated 14.12.2022 respondent no.1/accused has been enlarged on regular bail by trial court.
Victim X vs Prasoon on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176227068/
1 4. Learned counsel for applicant submits that FIR itself shows that respondent no. 1 tried to tamper with the evidence.
Sufficient evidence is available against the respondent no. 1 for violating the terms and conditions imposed by the trial court while granting bail to him.
After releasing on bail applicant is regularly threatening her, therefore, she has lodged two FIRs against respondent no. 1.
She has filed an application under section 439(2) of Cr.P.C. before the trial court but the same was rejected vide impugned order dated 15.5.2023.
Hence this application has been filed.
5. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent no. 1 submits that prosecutrix is continuously lodging false FIRs against him, he has also lodged FIR against the prosecutrix/petitioner.
Prosecutrix herself is not appearing before the trial court for recording her evidence.
The applicant has never tried to tamper with the evidence or threat to the prosecutrix.
Hence application deserves to be dismissed.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

7. From perusal of the order of the trial court, it appears that trial is pending for recording evidence of prosecutrix but due to non appearance of prosecutrix, her statement could not be recorded till now and petitioner/prosecutrix herself is causing delay in trial.
Both the parties lodged reports against each other due to their previous enmity and they are responsible for their acts and accordingly police has registered offence on the basis of said FIRs.
Therefore, it cannot be said that respondent no. 1 is misusing the liberty of bail which was given to him by the trial court.

8. In the case of Daulatram Vs. State of Haryana in 1995 (1) SCC Page 349, the apex Court has held as under:-
"Very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order directing the cancellation of the bail, already granted.

entities.text: Daulatram Vs. State of Haryana in 1995 (1) SCC Page 349
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Generally speaking, the grounds for cancellation of bail, broadly (illustrative and not exhaustive) are: interference or attempt to interfere with the due course of administration of justice or evasion or attempt to evade the due course of justice or abuse of the concession granted to the accused in any manner.
The satisfaction of the Court, on the basis of material placed on the record of the case, possibility of the accused absconding is yet another reason justifying the cancellation of bail.

However, bail once granted should not be cancelled in a mechanical manner without considering whether any supervening circumstances have rendered it no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow the accused to retain his freedom by enjoying the concession of bail during the trial."
9.

Looking to the aforesaid legal position, this Court is of the view that nothing has been brought on record by the learned counsel for the applicant on the basis of which bail granted to the respondent No.1/accused by the trial court can be cancelled.
10. Resultantly, the present application, filed under Section 439(2) of Cr.P.C, by the applicant is hereby dismissed.
